summary: The Netherlands does not record ethnicity. CBS publishes suspects of sexual and violent crimes by nationality and by country of birth and origin, with rates, but never for crimes against children, and no national statistics give the origin of child victims. Trafficking figures give victims and suspects by nationality; neglect, homicide and online abuse have no origin data.

european_title: Not recorded by any Dutch source
european_note: Dutch statistics record nationality and origin based on country of birth of the person and their parents, never ethnicity. 'Born in the Netherlands to Dutch-born parents' and 'origin elsewhere in Europe' are the closest groups to ethnic Europeans, but they are birth-country proxies: they include people of any descent and leave out ethnic Europeans born outside Europe.
proxy_note: The Netherlands records nationality and origin by country of birth, never ethnicity. Every group below is a proxy, not ethnicity.

harms.label: Sexual offences (suspects, all victims)
harms.intro: CBS registered 3,740 suspects of sexual offences in 2025, by nationality, for victims of all ages. The National Rapporteur's monitor of sexual violence against children (2020-2024) has no origin variable for victims or suspects.

victims.text: No national statistics give the nationality or origin of child victims.

perpetrators.scope: Netherlands, registrations of suspects of sexual offences, victims of all ages, 2025
perpetrators.rate_reason: CBS does not publish rates by nationality for this table.
perpetrators.share_note: CBS rounds counts to tens. Foreign = total minus Dutch minus stateless/unknown, calculated here. Most frequent foreign nationalities: pools 120, syrisch 100, roemeens 70, marokkaans 60, turks 50. Registrations of suspects, not unique people or convictions; includes suspects with no address in the Netherlands. Not child-victim-specific. Nationality, not ethnicity: Dutch statistics never record ethnic origin. 'Dutch' includes naturalised citizens.

cross.text: Suspect tables are not split by the victim's age or origin, so no victim-by-suspect table exists.

harms.label: Violence and assault (suspects, all victims)
harms.intro: No national statistics give the origin of children who are victims of violence. CBS publishes suspects of violent crimes (32,360 in 2025) by country of birth and origin with rates, and suspects of assault (23,450) by nationality, all for victims of all ages.

victims.text: No national statistics give the nationality or origin of child victims.

perpetrators.rate_label: suspects per 10,000 residents of the same group
perpetrators.rate_note: Rates as published by CBS (per 10,000 registered residents; crude, not adjusted for age).
perpetrators.share_note: CBS origin (herkomst) is based on the country of birth of the person and their parents; it is not ethnicity, and people born in the Netherlands to Dutch-born parents can be of any descent. Violent crimes cover all victims, mostly adults; not child-victim-specific. Counts rounded to tens.

cross.text: Suspect tables are not split by the victim's age or origin, so no victim-by-suspect table exists.

data.rate_label: suspects per 10,000 residents of the same group
data.rate_note: Rates as published by CBS. No combined rate is published for origin outside Europe; by region: Turkey 40, Morocco 63, Suriname 52, Dutch Caribbean 84, Indonesia 10, other non-European 36 per 10,000.
data.share_note: CBS origin (herkomst): origin 'Netherlands' is people born in the Netherlands to Dutch-born parents (the same 14,250 suspects as in the main block); 'elsewhere in Europe' is people born elsewhere in Europe or, if born in the Netherlands, with a parent born there. Origin outside Europe adds Turkey, Morocco, Suriname, Dutch Caribbean, Indonesia and other countries, calculated here. A birth-country proxy, not ethnicity.

harms.intro: Veilig Thuis and youth-protection statistics publish no usable origin variable; CBS has discontinued the migration-background breakdown of youth-protection data (all values empty in table 85100NED).

harms.label: Homicide
harms.intro: CBS publishes homicide victims by age (with an under-20 band) but no origin of victims or suspects in its current tables.

victims.text: Homicide victims are published by age and sex only.

perpetrators.text: No origin of homicide suspects is published separately; homicide is included in the violent-crime suspect figures (see Physical abuse).

harms.label: Human trafficking
harms.intro: 952 possible victims of human trafficking were reported to the national coordination centre (CoMensha) in 2025, 90 of them minors. Police and the Royal Marechaussee had 202 trafficking suspects in view, 11 of them minors. Nationality is published for all ages and forms together.

victims.scope: Netherlands, possible trafficking victims registered by CoMensha, all ages, 2025
victims.share_note: Registrations by CoMensha, an NGO that acts as the national coordination centre, analysed by the National Rapporteur. The group counts add up to 950, two fewer than the total. Among the 44 minors who were victims of criminal exploitation, 35 were Dutch. Nationality, not ethnicity.

perpetrators.scope: Netherlands, trafficking suspects in police and KMar investigations, 2025
perpetrators.share_note: 150 Dutch, 13 Romanian, 9 Bulgarian and 5 Moroccan suspects; foreign = 202 minus 150, calculated here (it may include a few of unknown nationality). People tried in 2021-2025 were 63% born in the Netherlands (68% in 2025). Nationality, not ethnicity: Dutch statistics never record ethnic origin. 'Dutch' includes naturalised citizens.

cross.text: No table links victim and suspect nationality.

harms.label: Online child sexual exploitation
harms.intro: The police child-abuse-material team identified 1,595 victims and 1,280 suspects over 2020-2024 (National Rapporteur monitor), with no nationality or origin.

victims.text: Identified victims are not published by any origin variable.

perpetrators.text: Suspects are not published by any origin variable.

breakdown.why: CBS gives registrations of suspects of sexual offences by nationality (3,740 in 2025; Dutch 2,880), all victims and rounded to tens. The National Rapporteur's monitor of sexual violence against children has no origin variable for victims or suspects. Heritage points are 0 under the paired-data rule: no published cross-table of child victim and offender heritage for the same cases.

No victim origin. CBS gives assault suspects by nationality and suspects of violent crime by origin (born in the Netherlands, rest of Europe, Turkey, Morocco, Suriname, ...) with rates per 10,000 residents, all victims. Heritage points are 0 under the paired-data rule: no published cross-table of child victim and offender heritage for the same cases.

CBS gives homicide victims by age only; no origin of victims or suspects is published in current tables. Heritage points are 0 under the paired-data rule: no published cross-table of child victim and offender heritage for the same cases.

The National Rapporteur's 2025 figures give possible victims by nationality group (952; 224 Dutch; 90 minors) from CoMensha (an NGO) registrations, police and KMar suspects by nationality (202; 150 Dutch) and people tried by country of birth. All forms of trafficking. Heritage points are 0 under the paired-data rule: no published cross-table of child victim and offender heritage for the same cases.

Police identify victims of child sexual abuse material (1,595 over 2020-2024) but publish no origin of victims or suspects. Heritage points are 0 under the paired-data rule: no published cross-table of child victim and offender heritage for the same cases.

components.name: Victim heritage
components.full: Official data by harm that separately identify ethnic European children (e.g. White non-Hispanic, White British) alongside every other group, self-reported or official, few unknowns. Broad categories that lump ethnic Europeans with others get partial credit; proxies (nationality, citizenship, migration background, country of birth) at most 9.4 points.

components.name: Perpetrator heritage
components.full: Same standard for perpetrators: not perceived, few unknowns, ethnic Europeans separately identified. Proxies at most 9.4 points.

components.name: Coverage and missing data
components.full: Over 90% of the population covered, under 10% unknown

components.name: Rates and linkage
components.full: Rates per 100,000 possible, and victim heritage linked to perpetrator heritage

score.gold_standard: 100% means a country publishes data that separately identifies ethnic Europeans, both as perpetrators (so one can tell when they disproportionately harm a group) and as child victims (so one can tell when ethnic European children are disproportionately harmed), alongside every other group, linked victim to perpetrator, for every harm. Heritage points require that link as a published cross-table for the same child cases. One-sided data scores 0 for heritage.
score.rules: Heritage is 75 of every 100 points and is awarded only for a published cross-table that records child victim heritage and offender heritage for the same cases. One-sided data scores 0 for heritage. Coverage is 10, rates 7.5 and access 7.5. Proxies such as nationality or migration background earn at most a quarter of the heritage points, and only when that pair is published. A published “White” category that merges Hispanic people or another group, so ethnic Europeans cannot be isolated, is scored as a proxy under the same cap. A country with no real ethnicity data is capped at 25%. Neglect is not part of the score.
score.why: The Netherlands scores 12% on the stricter scale (0-20%). Heritage points are 0 because there is no published cross-table of child victim and offender heritage for the same cases. One-sided data earns no heritage credit. CBS publishes suspects of sexual and violent crimes by nationality and by origin (born in the Netherlands, rest of Europe and other regions), with rates, but never for crimes against children and never for victims. Trafficking figures give victims and suspects by nationality; other child harms have no origin data.
score.weights_id: harm weights of 24 Nov 2026 (homicide 27.78, sexual abuse 22.22, sex trafficking 22.22, physical abuse 16.67, online exploitation 11.11); paired-data rule: heritage points only for a published child victim×offender cross-table

paired_child.basis: No published cross-table of child victim and offender heritage for the same cases. One-sided data scores 0 for heritage.

Groups not listed have no data for that harm; the explorer should grey them out rather than offer an empty combination.
